title: Linkability of sensor telemetry data
description: Continuous collection of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps enables linking of data points to create comprehensive user profiles revealing movement patterns, daily routines, and health status.
assumptions: Data is stored and processed in a way that allows correlation across time and data types

title: Identifiability through biometric and location data
description: The combination of GPS position, timestamps, and biometric data (heart rate) can uniquely identify the user, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is not sufficiently anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensor data
description: Sensor telemetry data (heart rate, GPS, steps) could be accessed by unauthorized parties through device compromise, network interception, or backend system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Security controls may be insufficient to protect data in transit and at rest

title: Data aggregation revealing sensitive patterns
description: Aggregation of multiple data types (heart rate, steps, GPS, timestamps) over time reveals sensitive information beyond individual data points, such as health conditions, lifestyle patterns, and location habits.
assumptions: Data is retained and aggregated over extended periods

title: User unawareness of data collection scope
description: Users may not be fully aware of the extent of data being collected, how long it is retained, who has access to it, or how it may be used for secondary purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may be unclear or users may not read them carefully

title: Excessive Data Collection and Transfer
description: The wearable device collects and transfers detailed sensor data (GPS traces, exercise sessions, timestamps, device ID) to the companion app. This may exceed the minimality principle if all this data is not strictly necessary for the app's core functionality, representing an avoidable data disclosure.
assumptions: Assuming the app does not require all sensor data types for its primary function

title: Device and Location Identifiability
description: GPS traces combined with device ID and timestamps can uniquely identify individuals and their movement patterns. This data enables re-identification even if other identifiers are removed.
assumptions: GPS data has sufficient precision to identify specific locations and movement patterns

title: Cross-Data Linkability
description: Exercise sessions and GPS traces from this flow can be linked with other data sources (e.g., social media, health records, other apps) to build comprehensive user profiles, enabling inference of sensitive information.
assumptions: User data exists in multiple systems that could be correlated

title: User Unawareness of Data Sync Scope
description: Users may not be fully aware of what sensor data is being synced, how frequently, or what metadata (timestamps, device ID) is included in the transfer to the companion app.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain the scope of data synchronization

title: Limited User Control Over Data Transfer
description: Users may lack granular control over which sensor data types are synced to the companion app, or may not be able to selectively disable certain data transfers while maintaining app functionality.
assumptions: App settings do not provide fine-grained control over data synchronization

title: Linkability of health data to user identity
description: Calorie intake, meal, and weight entries logged by the user can be linked to their specific identity through the app account, enabling correlation of health data with the individual user.
assumptions: User account system links entries to specific user profiles

title: Identifiability through health data entries
description: The user can be identified from their logged health data (calories, meals, weight) which is associated with their account in the companion app.
assumptions: App maintains user accounts with identifiable information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: Sensitive health information (calorie intake, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or insecure transmission.
assumptions: App may have security vulnerabilities or data may be transmitted insecurely

title: Data aggregation revealing health patterns
description: Individual health entries (calories, meals, weight) can be aggregated over time to reveal detailed patterns about the user's health status, eating habits, lifestyle, and potential medical conditions.
assumptions: App stores historical data and may aggregate or analyze it

title: Unawareness of data sharing and usage
description: User may not be fully aware of how their health data (calories, meals, weight) is being used, shared with third parties, or what inferences can be drawn from it after entry.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not clearly explain data usage or user may not read it

title: Lack of user control over health data
description: User may have limited ability to control, modify, or delete their logged health data once entered into the companion app, or to opt out of certain data processing activities.
assumptions: App may not provide comprehensive data management controls

title: Excessive Health Data Collection
description: The companion app may collect and store more health data than necessary (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) without clear justification for each data element, violating the data minimality principle.
assumptions: App collects all health metrics without granular user control or purpose limitation

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Log Store
description: The health log store containing sensitive personal health data could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, authentication weaknesses, or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Data store has standard security controls that may have gaps

title: Health Data Identifiability
description: Health logs (weight history, exercise sessions, calorie intake) contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Health data is stored with user identifiers or can be linked to user accounts

title: User Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Users may not be fully aware of what health data is being stored, how long it is retained, or what purposes it serves beyond the immediate app functionality.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data storage practices

title: Health Data Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Storage of health data may not comply with applicable regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) regarding data protection, retention periods, and user rights for health information.
assumptions: Health data is subject to specific regulatory requirements
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and app classification

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The app writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the location history store. This may collect more location data than strictly necessary for the app's functionality, violating the minimality principle. Continuous location tracking could be considered implicit disclosure beyond what users reasonably expect.
assumptions: Location history is stored for purposes beyond immediate app functionality

title: Location Data Enables User Identification
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources. Location patterns are highly personal and can uniquely identify users.
assumptions: Location data is stored with sufficient granularity to enable identification

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History Store
description: The location history store containing GPS traces and timestamps could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or compromised credentials.
assumptions: Data store has potential security vulnerabilities or access control weaknesses

title: Users Unaware of Continuous Location Tracking
description: Users may not be fully aware that their GPS location is being continuously tracked and stored in the location history store, or may not understand the extent of data collection.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate continuous location tracking

title: Location Data Enables Cross-Context Linking
description: Location history with timestamps can be linked to other data about the user across different contexts, enabling comprehensive profiling of user behavior and movements.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with other user data sources

title: Cross-session health data linkability
description: The health log store provides calorie, weight, and exercise data across multiple sessions to the analytics service, enabling the linking of user activities over time to build comprehensive health profiles. This linkability could reveal patterns about user health conditions, lifestyle changes, and behavioral trends that may not have been intended to be connected.
assumptions: Health logs contain session identifiers or timestamps that allow correlation across different data access events

title: Health data identifiability
description: Calorie, weight, and exercise logs stored in DS1 may contain or enable derivation of personally identifiable information. When combined across sessions for health-condition analysis, these data points could uniquely identify individuals or reveal sensitive health conditions.
assumptions: Health metrics combined with session data can be used to identify or profile specific individuals

title: Excessive health data disclosure for analytics
description: The data store transfers all health logs (calorie, weight, exercise) to the analytics service. This may violate the minimality principle if not all data types are strictly required for the stated health-condition analysis purpose, resulting in unnecessary disclosure of personal health information.
assumptions: The analytics service may not require all three data types (calorie, weight, exercise) for all analysis scenarios
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether all data types are minimally necessary for the stated purpose

title: User unawareness of cross-session health analytics
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs are being read across multiple sessions for analytics purposes. The data store disclosure to the analytics service may occur without explicit user knowledge or consent for this specific use case.
assumptions: Users may not have been informed about cross-session analytics or may not understand the scope of data being analyzed

title: Cross-session location data linking
description: The Health Analytics Service queries location history across multiple sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, enabling linkage of otherwise separate data points into a comprehensive behavioral profile.
assumptions: Location history from different sessions is being combined and correlated

title: Enhanced identifiability through pattern analysis
description: Deriving movement patterns and daily routines from location history increases the identifiability of individuals, as behavioral patterns can be used to uniquely identify users even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Location patterns are sufficiently unique to identify individuals

title: Non-minimal data collection for analytics
description: The analytics service collects and processes location history across sessions to derive patterns, which may exceed the minimal data necessary for the stated purpose, constituting avoidable data disclosure.
assumptions: Full location history across sessions is being collected rather than aggregated or anonymized data

title: User unawareness of pattern derivation
description: Users may not be aware that their location history is being analyzed across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, beyond simple location tracking.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly explain cross-session pattern analysis

title: Lack of user control over pattern analysis
description: Users likely have no control over whether their location history is analyzed across sessions to derive behavioral patterns, or what patterns are derived and how they are used.
assumptions: No user settings or opt-out mechanisms for pattern analysis

title: Health condition inference reveals personal identity
description: The analytics service generates health-condition risk indicators and routine summaries that are inherently personal data. If this data is intercepted or improperly accessed during transmission to the app, the identity and health status of the data subject could be revealed, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Health analytics data contains personally identifiable or inferable information about the user's health status

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health analytics during transmission
description: Sensitive health insights (risk indicators, trend flags, routine summaries) transmitted from the analytics service to the mobile app could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the data flow lacks proper encryption or access controls.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over a network that could be intercepted without adequate security measures

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data transmission
description: The transmission of sensitive health analytics data may not comply with applicable regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) if proper cybersecurity risk management practices are not implemented, including encryption, access controls, and audit logging for this data flow.
assumptions: Health data is subject to regulatory compliance requirements that mandate specific security controls
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific health data classification

title: User unaware of inference methodology and accuracy
description: Users may not understand how eating-disorder or diabetes risk indicators are inferred, the confidence levels of these predictions, or the data sources used. This could lead to misinterpretation of health signals and inappropriate health decisions.
assumptions: The app displays inferred health conditions without clear explanation of methodology, confidence scores, or data provenance.

title: Sensitive health information deducible from displayed trends
description: The displayed trends and condition indicators could allow deduction of more specific health information than intended. For example, eating patterns shown could reveal specific disordered eating behaviors beyond the general risk indicator.
assumptions: The dashboard displays granular trend data that could be analyzed to infer additional sensitive health information.

title: Non-compliance with healthcare regulations for displaying medical risk indicators
description: Displaying eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals may trigger regulatory requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, medical device regulations) that the app may not fully comply with, including requirements for accuracy disclaimers, user consent, and data handling procedures.
assumptions: The app displays health risk indicators that could be considered medical information subject to healthcare regulations.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and whether the app is classified as a medical device.

title: Transfer of sensitive health and location data to third-party cloud provider
description: The full health and location dataset is being transferred to an external cloud hosting provider (EE2). This constitutes explicit data disclosure across a system boundary. The minimality principle should be evaluated: is the full dataset strictly required, or could anonymized/aggregated data suffice?
assumptions: The cloud provider is a known third party with access to the complete dataset

title: Increased identifiability risk through third-party data hosting
description: Health and location data combined with analytics models at the cloud provider increases the risk of re-identification. Third-party providers may have additional data sources that could be linked to identify individuals.
assumptions: Cloud provider may have access to other datasets or metadata that could enable identification

title: Linkability of health data with other data at cloud provider
description: Health and location data hosted at the cloud provider could be linked with other data the provider collects or processes, creating comprehensive profiles of individuals across different contexts.
assumptions: Cloud provider may process or store other personal data that could be linked

title: Loss of individual control over health and location data
description: By transferring data to a third-party cloud provider, individuals lose direct control over their sensitive health and location information. The cloud provider's policies and practices determine how data is accessed, used, and protected.
assumptions: Individuals have limited visibility into or control over third-party data handling practices

title: Individuals unaware of third-party data transfer
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health and location data is being transferred to and hosted by a third-party cloud provider, or how this data will be used beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate third-party data transfers
